references.text: The description of the altar of burnt offering that God commanded Moses to make, the same altar that is now to be placed in front of the entrance to the tabernacle.
The account of how Bezalel actually made the altar of burnt offering (מִזְבַּח הָעֹלָה) according to God's instructions.
Instructions regarding the daily burnt offerings that were to be offered on this altar at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
The fulfillment of this command, where Moses actually placed the altar of burnt offering in front of the entrance to the tabernacle.
Instructions concerning the burnt offering that was to be brought at the entrance to the tent of meeting (אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד), where the altar stood.
A reference to the altar of burnt offering standing in front of the entrance to the tent of meeting.
The New Testament perspective on the altar as a type of Christ's sacrifice, where the author contrasts the Old Testament altar with the new one in Christ.
The placement of the altar in 40:6 is theologically anchored in 29:42 as the fixed meeting place between God and Israel.
The ritual in Lev 4:18 presupposes and confirms the placement of the altar of burnt offering established in Exod 40:6.
The cleansing ritual in Lev 14:11 confirms that the entrance to the tent is the central place for offerings, as indicated by the location of the altar of burnt offering.
The placement of the guilt offering in Lev 19:21 confirms that 'the entrance' is the common meeting place for all types of offerings, including the burnt offering.
